faq.a: A rich banking family of Florence who led the city for much of the 1400s and later. They paid for art, buildings and scholarship, and two Medici became popes.
A person or group who pays an artist, writer or scientist to make work. Renaissance patrons included bankers, rulers, guilds and the Church.
A Renaissance way of thinking that studied ancient Greek and Roman writers and celebrated human abilities like reason, art and learning.

faq.q: How did Brunelleschi build the dome?
faq.a: He used a clever herringbone pattern of bricks and two shells, one inside the other, so the dome could rise without a huge wooden frame underneath. It was finished in 1436.

faq.q: Did the Renaissance happen only in Italy?
faq.a: No. It began in Italian city-states, then spread to Flanders, France, Germany, England and beyond. It also drew on learning kept and developed in the Islamic world and Byzantium.

facts: Brunelleschi's dome of Florence Cathedral was completed in 1436.
The word Renaissance comes from French and means rebirth.

quiz.say: What does the word Renaissance mean?
quiz.why: It means rebirth, the revival of ancient learning and art.

wrong.1: Painting was part of it, but the word means rebirth.
wrong.2: Banks paid for it, but the word means rebirth.

quiz.why: Patrons like the Medici paid artists and builders to create.

wrong.1: Paints were made from pigments; a patron is a person.
wrong.2: Ruins inspired artists, but a patron is a supporter.
